name: Halo laser (hybrid fractional)

lead: Halo is a hybrid fractional laser that combines two wavelengths in a single treatment. People use it to get a more even skin tone and smoother texture, and to soften sun damage, pigment and scars.

It works by creating microscopic columns of controlled injury, one set shallow and one deeper, which the skin heals by remodeling. Registered studies are small: a 15-person study of facial and neck photoaging, a 34-person study of conditions including dyschromia and photodamage, and a trial of a hybrid fractional laser for acne scars in skin of color.

paras: Halo is done in a dermatology or aesthetic clinic, usually as a single session or a short series. Downtime depends on how deep the settings are set, so people plan recovery around the chosen intensity. Results build as skin remodels over the following weeks.

Hyperpigmentation after laser treatment is a studied concern, particularly in darker skin tones. Redness, swelling and peeling occur while skin heals, and downtime varies with settings. It is a clinic-only procedure, and people with active skin infections or a tendency to scar should raise that with the provider.

chain: Even tone, smoother scars and texture
angle.text: Halo combines ablative and non-ablative wavelengths in one pass so skin resurfaces at two depths and remodels, evening tone and smoothing scars and texture. People use it for sun damage, scars and pigment, and registered studies of 15 to 34 people have examined it.

lead: Halo is a hybrid fractional laser, a category that combines an ablative and a non-ablative fractional wavelength in a single pass, aimed at photoaging, scars and pigment. Source material for this entry is thin, consisting of clinical trial registrations that name the Profile Halo mixed fractional laser or hybrid fractional lasers generally [1][2].

Registered studies are small: a 15-person study of facial and neck photoaging with the Profile Halo [1], a 34-person study of various skin conditions including dyschromia and photodamage [2], and a trial of a hybrid fractional laser for acne scars in skin of color [3].
infobox: Photoaging, dyschromia, acne scars, skin laxity

paras: A completed study registered in 2015 evaluated the Profile Halo mixed fractional laser for facial and neck photoaging in 15 participants [1]. A completed 2016 study (n=34) addressed dyschromia and photodamaged skin [2]. A 2019 study tested a hybrid fractional laser on off-face skin laxity in 7 participants [4], and a recruiting trial from 2023 (n=50) examines acne scars with pigmentation risk in skin of color [3]. Results are not reported in the registrations used here, and no larger controlled evidence is cited.
